name: play-button-mirrors-core-pause
description: The play control's checked state always agrees with the core's pause flag, in both running and paused states.

steps.name: playing
steps.note: mpv brings a fresh file up playing, so the running state is the state the dialog opens into and needs no press to reach.
Back to running, so both states are checked rather than only the one the click produced.

steps.name: playing
steps.note: Every assertion is evaluated against the FINAL state, so the last thing that happens is the agreement under test rather than an intermediate one.

assertions.note: updatePlayIcon() ends with btnPlay_->setChecked(running) (PlayerShell.cpp:865), so checked == true means running. This is the state the button used to have no handle on at all - the glyph was a function pointer and checked was pinned false on every build, which would have made any assertion here unfailable.

The other half of the pair. The button is a view of the core, never a second source of truth: updatePlayIcon() re-reads surface_->isPlaying() rather than trusting its own cached playing_, because a PiP hand-back can leave the two disagreeing.
The paused state the two presses passed through. If the core had never left paused, the checked == true assertion above would still hold on a player whose play control and core never agreed at all.
